column13: guidance
Cash kept in the office for small purchases.
Main business current account. Rename to your bank, e.g. 'DBS Current'.
Savings or fixed-deposit account for reserves.
Multi-currency account (e.g. Wise / Airwallex). Record the SGD value of each movement.
Money collected by Stripe / PayPal that has not yet been paid out to the bank.
SYSTEM. Choose this when a customer pays one of your invoices (put the invoice # in Reference).
Money owed to the company that is not a customer invoice, e.g. a grant approved but not yet received.
SYSTEM. Costs paid in advance (filled automatically when you 'spread' a payment over months).
Refundable deposits, e.g. office rental or utilities deposit.
Money advanced to staff or directors that they will repay or account for.
Laptops, servers, monitors above the capitalisation threshold. Also add them to the asset register.
Desks, chairs, printers, AV equipment. Also add them to the asset register.
Office renovation and fit-out works. Also add them to the asset register.
Purchased or capitalised software, trademarks, domain portfolios. Add them to the asset register.
SYSTEM. Reduces the value of assets over time (from the asset register). Normally a negative balance.
SYSTEM. Choose this when you pay a supplier bill recorded in Bills (put the bill # in Reference).
Costs already incurred but not yet billed (usually used by your accountant in the Journal).
Company credit card. Record card spending as Money Out from this account; paying the card bill is a transfer from the bank.
SYSTEM. Choose this when you pay staff their net salary (after the pay run).
SYSTEM. Choose this when you pay CPF Board (CPF, SDL and self-help group funds).
Pay a founder or director has agreed to defer, owed to them until paid (PRD-001 B.7); a sub-ledger per person.
Staff paid for company expenses personally: record the expense as Money Out from this account; reimbursing them is a transfer from the bank to this account.
SYSTEM. GST owed to IRAS (or refundable). Choose this when you pay GST to, or receive a GST refund from, IRAS.
Corporate income tax owed to IRAS. Choose this when paying corporate tax.
SYSTEM. Customer money received in advance for future months (filled automatically when revenue is spread).
Advance payments / retainers received before any invoice. Apply them later with a Journal.
Money lent to the company by founders or shareholders, and repayments of it.
Bank or government-assisted loans (principal only; interest goes to Interest expense).
Investor money received under a SAFE or convertible note, before it converts into shares.
Not sure where something goes? Use this, then ask your accountant. Must be cleared before closing a month.
Money received from shareholders for ordinary shares.
Money received from investors for preference shares.
SYSTEM. Accumulated profits / (losses) of previous years. Enter the opening balance here (negative if losses).
Dividends paid to shareholders.
A founder's balance waived as a shareholder (FR-EQ-07): equity, not income.
Recurring software / platform subscription fees (monthly or annual plans).
Consulting, implementation, training and other service fees.
Fixed-price or milestone-based AI / software project work.
Any other income from customers.
Refunds or discounts given to customers (reduces revenue).
Servers, cloud computing, storage and hosting used to run the product for customers.
Usage-based AI model / API fees and other third-party services embedded in the product.
Freelancers or subcontractors working directly on customer projects.
Card / Stripe / PayPal fees on customer payments.
Salaries of staff who deliver customer projects or support (set by the pay run).
Other costs directly linked to delivering to customers.
Gross salaries of product, engineering and data staff (set by the pay run).
Gross salaries of sales, marketing and partnerships staff.
Gross salaries of management, finance, HR and admin staff.
SYSTEM. Employer's share of CPF (calculated by the pay run).
SYSTEM. SDL (calculated by the pay run) and foreign worker levies.
Medical, insurance, wellness and other staff benefits.
Fees paid to non-executive directors.
Recruiter fees, job ads, work-pass application fees.
Courses, certifications, conferences for staff development.
Online ads, SEO, content, marketing agencies.
Trade shows, sponsorships, PR, marketing materials.
Commissions and referral fees paid to third parties.
Internal software subscriptions: email, office suite, design, developer tools.
Small IT items below the capitalisation threshold: keyboards, cables, small devices.
External R&D services, data labelling, testing services.
Office rent or co-working desk membership.
Electricity, water, gas for the office.
Mobile plans, broadband, phone lines.
Stationery, pantry, printing, postage.
Repairs of office and equipment.
Bookkeeping, tax filing, audit and payroll services.
Lawyers: contracts, fundraising documents, IP.
Company secretary, ACRA filing fees, licences and permits.
Business and technical consultants (not delivering customer projects).
Business insurance: public liability, professional indemnity, cyber, D&O.
Bank service charges and transfer fees.
Taxis, ride-hailing, parking, public transport for business.
Flights, hotels and allowances for business trips.
Business meals and client entertainment.
SYSTEM. Monthly depreciation from the asset register.
Amortisation of intangible assets (via the Journal).
Small expenses that do not fit another category.
Grants and wage subsidies received from government agencies.
Interest earned on bank deposits.
SYSTEM. Exchange-rate and small rounding differences when invoices / bills are settled.
Month-end revaluation of open foreign-currency items and balances (FR-GL-04); reverses on the first day of the next period.
Profit or loss when you sell or scrap an asset (via the Journal). (7040 in the workbook: moved because 7040 is unrealised FX in Fyniq, PRD-001 B.5)
Interest and fees on loans.
Late-payment penalties, fines and other non-deductible items.
Corporate income tax charge for the year (via the Journal).
